content:
Hello Team La Union, upon passing by Diversion Road I noticed that there are no safety signage especially speed limit knowing na maraming mga houses po and may ginagawa pong daanan. Wala pong nakalagay na one way or two way po ba kasi nadaan po ako sinasalubong na lang namin mha big truck tapos gigilid po kami.  

Sorry to say po napapansin ko kapag malapit na election dami po pinapagawa ang govt. Kung widening para saan? Pero hindi po napapansin ng govt ang safety ng mga tao since maraming mga pasaway din po na tao sa paligid. 

Wala po kasing alert man lang. Sobrang traffic na po  ang SFC. Hindi na po sasakyan ang problema daanan. Kasi kung alternative route meron naman kaso hindi po siya safe. Ginagawa pong free way ang diversion road. Mas maganda po sana kung may speed limit or safety signage and consistent po ang paghuli.  Sabi bawal po magpark along the street pero marami pong nakapark. 

Hindi ko rin po alam bakit wala rin pong water sa Sevilla area. Ano po ba ang problema? Wala po kasing explanation sa barangay.

Mabibilis po ang mga sasakyan sa diversion road especially sa gabi. Hindi lamg po street lights ang kailangan po kailangan din po ng traffic light or amber light na oppss slow down ako dito kasi intersection to, blocks.

Sana.mapagtuunan niyo po ng pansin hindi po kasi pwedeng.bahala na. Kaya po nating educate ang disiplina sa tao..kasi.matatakot naman po iyan.kapag consistent po ang rules.

Thank you.

offices.name: Office for Public Safety

events.content: Your feedback has been received by concern office. Please wait for futher updates.

Good day!

Thank you po for  informing these concerns. We will immediately inform the contractors to place speed limit or slow down signs on areas which are still under construction para po ma install na as soon as possible. With regard to the recommendation to install traffic lights, we are already working on it para po makainstall ng traffic lights sa mga strategic areas.  On enforcement naman po, we will coordinate with the PNP para mas consistent po ang enforcement duon. 

Lastly, we will also coordinate po sa mga concerned offices regarding po sa other concerns po na  na i raise.  Thank you.
This feedback is mark as completed. Thank You!

content: Good day po. Kami po ng pamilya ko ay bumisita po sa San Fernando, La Union para sa LTOP license ng kuya ko at ni papa. Nagdecide kami na kumain sa isang unliwings unli rice dyan sa Bayan po ninyo. At sinabi po ng crew na ishare ko na lang daw ang anak ko sa food kasi 2yrs old palang naman siya. Pero nagOrder ako ng hindi unli for my son…nuggets, fries & apple drink. Pero dahil nabusog na sa meryenda namin before kami kumain sa unli wings..hindi nabwasan ng anak ko yung inorder ko para saknya…pero dahil may word yung isang crew na ishare ko ang anak ko so naghimay po ako ng chicken para sa anak ko…pero hindi parin niya kinain kasi busog pa cguro siya…tapos sinabi ko sa crew kasi paalis na kami at paid na kami…So sabi ko itakeout na lang ang food ng anak ko pati drink kasi di pa niya nababawasan kasama nung hinimay ko na chicken…pero wala silang puso at consideration…pinakitaan kmi ng pangit na ugali. Babayaran ko raw yun kasi left over daw…paanong left over e hindi namn unlimited yung pagkain ng anak ko at hindi pa naman yun nababawasan paano yun naging leftover?kung food ko okay lang. E pagkain ng anak ko yun at pwd siyang magutom sa daan at hindi kami taga La Union…We are from Dagupan City, Pangasinan pa. Hindi pa ba sapat yung binayad namin at hindi pa nga kami nakakain masyado dahil senior citizens ang mga kasama namin both parents po nmin. Walang puso…walang manners..walang consideration. I want your office to take action about this since pauwi na po kami at may 2 yr old na bata at senior citizens na ksama at PWD ang sister ko. Hindi ko na po maharap ang magpunta sa office po ninyo. I just your office to know that isa itong kainan na ito na pwdng makasira sa image ng inyong municipality. At ayoko po na maulit itong mangyari sa iba pa ninyong bisita/turista. Sana po maunawaan niyo ako bilang isang ina at bilang isang anak din ng mga old aged people na talgang kelngan ng attention including ang ate ko na PWD po. Hindi ko po inexpect na ganito po ang dadanasin nmin sa San Fernando, La Union. At sinagot pa po ako ng manager ata yun na we did our best to serve you kahit hindi…very poor service po. Very humiliating ang dating…nagbayad ka na…napahiya ka pa. Para sigawan niya ako sa harap ng maraming taong kumakain na para bang sila pa ang agrabyado dito. Bayad na kami earlier dahil nagmamadali kami pinapatakeout ko na lang ang food ng anak ko dahil di niya pa nababawasan kahit yung drink niya…sbhin ba naman na ipakain ko sa anak ko yun e hindi naman kasama sa kanilang unlimited meal yun…pipilitin ko ang bata na kumain? Para lang sa hinimay na chicken na hindi bawas ng anak ko…magbabayad kami?ni hindi niya natikman yang unli na yan at may sarili siyang food at sinabi naman nila na pwd ko siyang ishare…Nkakaloka ang resto na to. Nagbayad ka na nga papahiyain ka pa at gusto ka pang lamangan. My goodness! Kung kami gusto namin patulan yan ginawa na namin…si papa ay retired army kung masama kami mga tao at mayabang nakarating na yan sa dapat niyang kalagyan pero hindi kami katulad nila na ampangit ng ugali…may takot kami sa Diyos at alam namin lumugar kahit na pinahiya kami hindi na kami sumagot at pinili na lang namin umalis at iwanan sknla ang pagkain ng anak ko na paid naman at di pa nababawasan. Pls po sana po maturuan ng leksyon ang mga taong ito. Dahil hindi po ako capable na makagawa ng action or magcomplajn dahil may anak ako at senior citizens na mga magilang at PWD ang sister ko. Kaya minabuti ko na lang po na kahit po dito man lang po sa online ay magkaroon po ng hustisya ang dinanas po namin sa inyong lugar. Maraming salamat po and God bless po. Here is my contact number po 09365448520. Pls update me po thank you so much 🙏🏻🙏🏻🙏🏻

Hello po.

With respect po sa mentally challenged persons, CHO po ang proper authority to cater those clients. 

Kami po sa CSWDO ay walang kakayahang makapanggamot ng ganitong uri ng kliyente sakaling sila ay hindi lucid sa mga oras na icacater namin sila.

Marapat pong icoordinate na lang sa CHO para sa nararapat at mas safe na aksyon.

Maraming Salamat po.

Hindi sa dinadown namin etong mentally challenged na person na ito. We have been putting up with him for the past years to the point na nakikiusap na kami sa family niya and sa barangay. Nagwawala and nagsusunog sa siya ng kung ano ano dito sa amin. If sa CHO ang right department, then we will talk to them. Hindi na namin alam kung saan lalapitan about this issue. Even the family doesn't want to coordinate with the barangay.

Magandang araw Ms. Angeline Morin. Magbibigay po kami ng feedback tungkol po sa inyong concern:

•	Nagconduct po ng home visit ang aming social worker sa naturang kliyente noong June 25, 2024 para ma-assess ang kanyang sitwasyon. Nakausap ng aming social worker ang kanyang kapatid na siyang kumopkop at nagbibigay ng kanyang pang-araw-araw na pangangailangan. Napag-alaman po namin na ang kliyente ay may iniinom na gamot para sa kanyang kondisyon, ngunit hindi ito regular. Gayon pa man, rinekomenda po ng social worker na ilapit ang kanyang case sa Psychiatrist para sa kanyang Psychological Evaluation sa Ilocos Training and Regional Medical Center (ITRMC) o sa Lorma Medical Center, upang matugunan pa lalo ang kanyang mga pangangailangan. 
•	Nakipag-ugnayan na rin ang aming opisina sa Baguio General Hospital and Medical Center ukol sa kanyang case. Ipinaalam na rin naming sa kanila na mag-Online Konsulta para ma-assess ng doktor kung ang kanyang case ay admissible.
•	Nirefer din namin sila sa aming programang AICS o Aid to Individual in Crisis Situation upang mabigyan ng tulong-pinansyal sa mga gastusin sa kanyang gamutan.
•	Ang CSWDO ay patuloy na sinusubaybayan ang case ng naturang kliyente.

Maraming salamat po.

I would like to express my concern regarding the service provided by La Union Electricity Company, Inc. (LUECO). It appears that they are not delivering a reliable electricity supply in Santiago Norte and the nearby barangays. Last week alone, we experienced between 12 to 20 power outages, and on average, 8 to 15 outages per week. Our city aspires to become a smart city in the future, but if LUECO's service continues to be this unreliable, achieving that goal may remain an empty promise.

content:
Wala bang magagawa ang city government sa water supply ng city? This is a pressing concern and wala naman improvement for so many years despite meetings with Primewater. 

Since Sept 11 walang water supply sa Carlatan. Wala ring advisory from Primewater. Hindi rin sila ma-contact sa hotlines nila. 

Mahirap din mag-request ng water delivery sa inyo kasi last time na nagpa-deliver ako pinagalitan ako ng foreman niyo. Hindi daw ako dapat nagrerequest kasi nakatira ako sa apartment. 

Eh saan pala kukuha ng tubig ang residents dito? Dapat mag-intervene ang city government because this is a very serious matter.

offices.name: Office of the City General Services Officer

events.content: Your feedback has been received by concerned office. Please wait for futher updates.

Magandang hapon po. Salamat sa inyong puna at sumbong. Nauunawaan namin ang inyong hinaing lalo't ang tubig ay isa sa ating pangunahing pangangailangan. Ang City government kasama ang Sangguniang Panlungsod ay patuloy na nakikipagugnayan sa mga ahensya na makakatulong sa ating problema sa tubig. Ilang beses naring naimbitahan ang Prime water upang sagutin at magpaliwanag sa kalagayan ng tubig sa ating siyudad. Gayunpaman, nais naming malaman ang buong detalye ukol sa pagtanggi ng isang kawani ng aming tanggapan sa inyong hiling. Kung maari po ay iniimbitahan namin kayo dito sa aming opisina 2nd floor GSO building para malaman namin ang iba pang impormasyon at paraan kung paano kami makakatulong. Salamat po.

Hindi po ako makakapunta during office hours kasi government employee din ako working from 8-5. Last month nag-request kami ng water delivery from the city kasi 2 weeks na walang binibigay ang Primewater. Noong una, pinagbigyan kami. Nung pangalawa ay hindi na. Nakatira daw kasi kami sa apartment. Ang binibigyan niyo lang daw ng tubig ay yung mga walang kakayanan na magbayad ng tubig. Hindi daw kami kasama dun kasi naka-apartment kami. Sabi ko dapat ayusin ng city government ang water supply sa siyudad kung ayaw niyo magbigay ng tubig kasi hindi naman kami hihingi kung maayos ang water supply. Ang sagot niya sakin ay dapat gawin yung may-ari ng apartment. Hindi namin ngayon alam saan kami kukuha ng tubig. Hindi responsive ang Primewater at Hindi rin ako maka-request sa City government.
Follow up on our concern.

Magandang hapon po. Naiintindihan namin ang hirap na maisabay ang mga personal na lakad sa oras ng trabaho. content:
Dear City of San Fernando, La Union,

I hope this email finds you well. I would like to raise some concerns and seek clarification regarding the veterinary services I received today from the City Veterinarian's Office.

Earlier today, I visited the City Veterinarian for my dog's 5-in-1 vaccine as it is the nearest to my residence. According to the Citizen's Charter page I consulted, it was indicated that these vaccinations are free of charge. Additionally, when I inquired at the provincial office two weeks ago, I was informed that the cost for the 5-in-1 vaccine was only ₱150. However, when I visited the City Veterinarian today, after administering the 5-in-1 vaccine, I was charged ₱450, which surprised me as this price is comparable to private clinics. As a student on a budget, I specifically chose the City Vet for this service based on the understanding that it would be more affordable.

Moreover, according to the City of San Fernando page, both the anti-rabies vaccine and deworming are supposed to be free of charge, yet when I asked about the next appointment for these, I was told there would be a ₱50 fee. Is this the standard practice?

Additionally, I was not provided with a vet card after my dog’s vaccination, and I was told that it would be given to me next week. Is this delay normal for issuing vaccination records?

Lastly, I observed that the deworming medicine and vitamins were dispensed from a single pump bottle, without any apparent cleaning in between use for different animals. This raises a concern for me, as I worry that my dog could be exposed to viruses if a previous dog receiving the same treatment had an illness. Could you please clarify if this is standard procedure and if there are measures in place to prevent cross-contamination?

I would appreciate it if you could address these concerns and provide clarity on whether these practices are consistent with the policies in place. Thank you for your time, and I look forward to your response.

Sincerely,
Belle

To whom it may concern: 

The collegians and the students of San Fernando La Union respectfully appeals for your immediate and urgent attention with careful consideration of the extreme heat currently affecting our city.

In light of the dangerous heat conditions that the city of San Fernando La Union is experiencing, authorities have issued advisories urging the public to stay indoors as much as possible, preventing heat-related illnesses and emergencies as these extreme conditions with the expected 37 up to 42-degree Heat Index.

Given these circumstances, we, the students, express our deep concern over the conduct of classes during the aforementioned dates, considering that it affects students’ academic performance and overall well-being. We humbly request the temporary suspension of face-to-face classes or the implementation of alternative learning modalities until tolerable and suitable weather conditions are conducive to students' learning environment. This proactive approach ensures the safety and health of every member belonging to the university.

We ask for immediate action for this appeal in the interest of our shared commitment to academic excellence and community care.

We hope for a positive response and we extend our deepest gratitude for your kindest consideration.

offices.name: Office of the City Health Officer

events.content: Your feedback has been received by concerned office. Please wait for futher updates.

Thank you, Kabsat for speaking up and sharing your concerns about the intense heat we’re all experiencing here in the City of San Fernando, La Union. Your active involvement shows how much you care about the health, learning, and overall well-being of our students.

The City Health Office (CHO), together with the City Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Office (CDRRMO), has been monitoring the heat index, which has ranged from 37°C to 42°C. According to PAGASA, this falls under the “extreme caution to danger” category. At this level, people are at risk for heat-related illnesses like cramps, exhaustion, or in worst cases, heat stroke. Fortunately, our local health facilities haven’t reported a major increase in such cases so far.
The heat index combines air temperature and humidity, and once it goes above 40°C, the risk of heat stress increases, especially for those directly exposed to the sun, like students walking to school or staying in poorly ventilated rooms. On the other hand, those in cooler, ventilated areas are much less affected. The key factors here are how long someone is exposed, their hydration, and their overall health.

Here are some simple but important tips for students and schools to stay safe:
•	Drink water every 20–30 minutes, even if you’re not thirsty.
•	Avoid staying under the sun between 10:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m.
•	Wear light-colored, loose clothes to help cool down.
•	Rest in shaded or breezy spots between classes.
•	If you feel dizzy, nauseous, or have a headache, let your school health officer know right away.
•	Use fans or open windows to cool classrooms or move classes to cooler times of the day.

The City Government continues to monitor the heat index closely. If it reaches dangerous levels of 42°C or higher and health data shows an increasing trend in heat-related illnesses, the CHO will quickly recommend flexible learning modalities to the City Mayor.
We make decisions based on data to ensure everyone’s health and education are protected. While we recognize your concerns and they’re completely valid, class suspensions need to be carefully considered alongside the actual health situation and academic needs.
Thank you again for your vigilance and care. Rest assured, we’re always working to ensure a safe, healthy, and supportive learning environment for all. Your suggestions will be shared with CHED and other appropriate agencies for quick action.

We’re all in this together, for a safer, healthier San Fernando.


References: 
Anderson, G. B., & Bell, M. L. (2011). Heat waves in the United States: mortality risk during heat waves and effect modification by heat wave characteristics in 43 US communities.
 Environmental Health Perspectives, 119(2), 210–218. https://doi.org/10.1289/ehp.1002313 Bouchama, A., Knochel, J. P., et al. (2007). Heatstroke. New England Journal of Medicine, 346(25), 1978–1988. 

https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMra011089 Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA). (2023). Heat Index Monitoring and Classification. 

https://www.pagasa.dost.gov.ph World Health Organization. (2018). Heat and Health: Technical Guidance for Health Systems. 

https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/WHO-WHE-PHE-EPE-18.05

doi.org

content:
GOOD DAY AND MABUHAY!

I would want to respectfully raise a health and sanitation concern here in our area at Upper Banks, Poro. 

Our neighbor, Ms. Dina Ramos, has an OVERFLOWING SEPTIC TANK that has been going on for months now. It has been emitting a severely foul, suffocating odor that affects several residents. Ms. Ramos and her family even intentionally lets her tank flow through the street going to an open lot with nearby residents (as seen in photos below). She even intentionally lets it flow during downpour of rain thinking it would not be noticed but the odor is so unbearable. We and our neighbors have peacefully approached Ms. Ramos of the septic tank but she did not bother to take action. The Barangay also did not take any action. 

The septic tank is already causing health problems I have been dealing with asthma and rhinitis now and our other neighbors experience nausea because of it. 

This is a clear violation of our environmental and sanitation laws and ordinances, and I believe with the months it has been on going, it ought to have penalty. 

Please do something about this as it poses great health danger in our community. 

I urge you to come visit, inspect and investigate. Try interviewing our neighbors. It is located beside Manabat Residence and Rilloraza Residence (the one that recently caught fire after the typhoon emong) in Upper Banks, Poro.

content:
Since late 2024 upto the entire year of 2025, garbage collection has been very intermittent in Barangay Poro most especially in Purok Banks and Fisherman's Village.  The reason according to the Barangay is the malfunctioning of the Garbage Collection Truck owned by the Barangay. Despite several repairs it was deemed unserviceable. Hence, the barangay sought the assistance of the City Government BUT problem is, the collection became very intermittent, internal puroks were not reached because apparently, the truck "was too big" to fit the streets of the purok.  

The barangay also announce that they made a loan with the City Government to purchase a new garbage truck. No update on this has ever been made. 

The intermittent garbage collection resulted to volumes of garbages along the streets. Although the city assists in collection, being it intermittent, the volume became too much for them to handle whenever they come to collect and there are left over garbages some puroks especially Banks and Fisherman's Village were never even visited. 

As of writing, the last collection in Purok Banks was December 23, 2025. 

We religiously pay Garbage Collection Fees... And we believe that we have to get the most of what we are paying however meager is the amount. 

We have entered another Calendar Year. Another year to pay taxes, garbage collection fees and the like. We deserve better service. 

While BAYANIHAN and PATIENCE is an ideal community value, i believe that this can also be abused to excuse the complacency of the government. 

WE NEED A PERMANENT SOLUTION TO THIS NOT JUST BAND AID SOLUTIONS. WE NEED TO REGULARIZE GARBAGE COLLECTION!!!!!

HINDI PWEDENG PASENSYA NA LAGI ...WE HAVE BEEN PATIENT ENOUGH FOR MORE THAN A YEAR DESPITE COMPLETE GARBAGE COLLECTION FEES PAID. IT IS UNFAIR FOR THE TAX PAYING COMMUNITY TO ENDURE THIS SECOND RATE SERVICE. 

WE ARE FED UP WITH APOLOGIES AND EXCUSES. WHAT WE NEED ARE THE FOLLOWING:,

1. DIRECT TO THE POINT ANSWER ON WHAT ARE THE PLANS TO PERMANENTLY RESOLVE GARBAGE COLLECTION ISSUE. 

2. TIMELINE ON WHEN THE ISSUE WILL BE RESOLVED

3. MONITORING AND EVALUATION MECHANISM FOR THE PLAN

4. RISK ASSESSMENT PLAN

PLEASE, THIS IS VERY URGENT. BAGONG TAON NA PO, GALAW GALAW PO.

content:
Concern regarding the use of public parking spaces around plaza

I am writing to formally raise a concern regarding the use of public parking spaces located around the Plaza—specifically in front of Saint William Church and the basketball court.
As you are aware, when there are no scheduled events, the basketball court is commonly utilized as a public parking area. However, earlier this morning, I experienced a very disappointing situation. When I attempted to park at the basketball court, I was blocked by parking attendants assigned in the area. I was asked where I work, and upon informing them that I am employed at BDO and not at City Hall, I was told that the area is reserved primarily for City Hall employees, and that non–City Government employees may only park there after all City Hall employees have secured parking.
This was extremely frustrating, especially since the area is a public space and should not be restricted exclusively for government employees. I was already running late for work, and this incident caused unnecessary delay and stress.
I respectfully request your attention to this matter, as these parking attendants—who appear to be unauthorized—are effectively prohibiting non–City Government employees from using public parking spaces around the Plaza. I believe this practice is unfair and contrary to the purpose of public facilities.
I sincerely hope that appropriate action or clarification can be made to ensure equal and fair access to public parking areas for all.
Thank you for your time and consideration.

Hello Mr. Corpuz, regarding your concern about the pharmacy denying a PWD discount on vitamins because of a missing paper prescription, we would like to clarify that the pharmacy actually followed the strict letters of the law. Under the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 10754 and Department of Health guidelines, vitamins and dietary supplements like Pharmaton Essentials are legally treated differently from regular over-the-counter medicines, meaning they strictly require a valid medical prescription from a doctor before any PWD discount or VAT exemption can be applied. Additionally, under Food and Drug Administration and Bureau of Internal Revenue rules, pharmacies cannot accept a mere smartphone photo of a past receipt or an old prescription because they are legally mandated to check, sign, and log the transaction directly onto a physical, hard-copy prescription and the PWD purchase booklet to prevent tax fraud and over-dispensing. While it is true that some other drugstores choose to be lenient and accept digital images, their laxity actually violates government regulations, the failure of others to follow the law does not excuse anyone else from compliance or turn an illegal shortcut into a right. Therefore, the drugstore was simply protecting its government license to operate, and to avoid any future inconvenience and successfully claim your 20% discount, please make sure to always bring three physical items to the counter: your original PWD ID card, your official PWD purchase booklet, and a fresh, hard-copy paper prescription from your attending physician. Thank you very much for time, we hope we have addressed your concerns.
This feedback is mark as completed. Thank You!

content:
This report is respectfully submitted to raise our concern regarding the collection of the environmental fee at Acapulco Beach at Brgy. San Francisco.During our recent visit, we rented a cottage and paid the required cottage rental fee. However, aside from the cottage payment, we were still required to pay an additional environmental fee per person, and we were also asked to declare the total number of attendees.

We would like to express our concern about this situation because we believe that since we already paid for the cottage rental, any environmental or maintenance-related fees should already be included in that payment. It seems unfair for customers to shoulder an additional environmental fee on top of the rental fee. In our opinion, the responsibility for paying the environmental fee should fall on the caretaker or owner of the cottage, as they are the ones operating and benefiting from the business within the area.

Furthermore, requiring customers to declare the number of attendees for the purpose of collecting environmental fees creates confusion and inconvenience. Clear and transparent policies regarding fees would help prevent misunderstandings and ensure fairness for visitors.

We respectfully request that the policy regarding the collection of environmental fees be reviewed and clarified. We hope that environmental fees will be managed directly by the cottage caretakers or owners rather than being charged separately to customers who have already paid for rentals. Our intention in raising this concern is to promote fairness, transparency, and a better experience for all visitors.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Kaisa mo kami sa pagpapalaganap ng adbokasiyang ito. Narito ang "Build a Go Bag" checklist upang maibahagi mo sa iyong mga kaibigan at kapitbahay, para mas marami pa tayong mahikayat na maghanda.

content:
**Public Concern Regarding Tricycle Fare Overcharging**

I would like to raise a concern regarding the implementation of tricycle fares in our area.

Many tricycle drivers are no longer following the official fare matrix. Even for very short distances, passengers are often charged double or even more than the standard fare. When passengers question the amount, some drivers become argumentative or disrespectful instead of explaining the basis of the fare.

Another concern is the fares being charged at night. Many drivers suddenly increase their rates to two or three times the regular fare. This raises an important question: **Is there an officially approved night differential for tricycle fares?** If there is, the public should be informed of the authorized rates. If there isn't, then arbitrary fare increases should not be allowed.

We respectfully ask the concerned local government unit and transport authorities to:

* Strictly enforce the official fare matrix.
* Ensure that tricycle drivers display the approved fare matrix where passengers can easily see it.
* Investigate complaints of excessive fare charging.
* Clarify whether a legally approved night differential fare exists and, if so, make the information readily available to the public.

Public transportation should be fair, transparent, and affordable for everyone. We hope the appropriate authorities will address this issue to protect both passengers and honest tricycle drivers who follow the rules.

Thank you for bringing your concerns about tricycle fare implementation to our attention. 

We acknowledge the issues raised regarding adherence to the official fare matrix, the conduct of some drivers when questioned about fares, and the reported fare increases during nighttime hours. 

Night Differential Fares: There are no officially approved night differential fares. However, the fare matrix is applicable from 5 a.m. to 9 p.m. only. After this period, the driver and passenger must agree on the fare.

Enforcement of Fare Regulations: We will intensify the enforcement of the existing fare matrix and ensure that all tricycle drivers are reminded of their obligation to display the approved fare rates prominently in their vehicles.

Overcharging Complaints: For any concerns about overcharging, passengers are encouraged to report violations to our office, specifically at the Public Assistance Desk Unit (PADU), or call 0938-639-9631 for immediate action.

Thank you for your concern and for helping us serve you better.

events.content: Your feedback has been received by concerned office. Please wait for futher updates.

Magandang araw po sa inyo. Nararamdaman at nauunawaan po namin ang inyong labis na pag-aalala para sa inyong negosyo na higit na 30 taon nang nagsisilbi sa ating lungsod. ALam po namin ang malaking sakripisyo at pagsubok na pinagdadaanan ng abwat pamilyang naapektuhan ng nagdaang sakuna. 
Nais po namin linawin at ipaliwanag ang mga hakbang at katotohanan ukol sa mga usaping inyong nabanggit:
1. Bilang ng mga Eatery at pwesto sa Temporary Market - Nais po naming ipaalam na hindi po nadagdagan ang mga eatery, bagkus ay nabawasan pa nga po ang bilang ng mga ito dahil ang iba ay hindi na nagtinda. Ang lahat ng mga nakapwesto ngayon sa temporary market ang mga naretain at dating eatery vendors na biktima rin ng sunog noong Enero 11, 2024. 
2. Proseso ng pagkuha ng Pwesto - Kaya po mahirap kumuha ng pwesto noon ay dahil occupied na ang lahat ng espasyo. Wala pong mga "baker" o paboritismo; nilipat lamang po ang mga legal at orihinal na vendors sa bagong temporary market upang muli kayong makapag-hanapbuhay matapos ang sakuna. 
3. Lamesa lang ang binigay na pwesto - Dahil po sa temporary lang naman ang establisyemento ay pare-parehong sukat lng ang naibigay sa inyo para po magkasya po kayong lahat at walang maiiwan. Magbabago din po ang pwesto nyo pag nakapagpatayo na po tayo ng ating bagong pamilihan. 
Ginagawa po ng pamunuan ang lahat ng aming makakaya upang mapanatili ang kalinisan at kaayusan ng pampublikong pamilihan. Subalit, hindi po ito kayang gawin ng pamunuan lamang - kailangan din po natin ang kooperasyon ng bawat vendor upang mapanatiling malinis, maayos, at maaliwalas ang ating paligid para sa mga namimili. 
Pinoprotektahan din namin ang kapakanan ng bawat vendor sa loob ng pamilihan. Sa katunayan po ay isinangguni na po namin ang usaping ito kay Mam Sally Medrano (LEBDO) ukol sa mga pumapasok na nagtitinda o nagpapadeliver mula sa labas. Ang naging paliwanag po ay hindi sila pwedeng pagbawalan dahil legal at nakarehistro ang kanilang negosyo. Bukod dito, choice o karapatan din po ng mga namimili at mismong mga tao sa market kung kanino nila gustong bumili o magpadeliver ng kanilang pagkain. 
Nauunawaan po namin ang higpit ng kumpetisyon lalo na sa pagdami ng mga mall at mga pagbabago sa merkado. Asahan ninyong patuloy na makikinig ang pamunuan upang higit pang mapaganda ang pasilidad at sistema para sa ikabubuti ng ating mga matatagal at tapat na vendors. 
Maraming salamat po sa inyong pang unawa at patuloy na pakikipagtulungan.

content: WATER CRISIS between Primewater and Metro Water District, the consumers are suffering. Our city is Overlooking this Water Crisis: Water supply, especially in places like San Fernando, is an ongoing indefinite struggle. We need long-term solutions for water scarcity, especially as tourism keeps growing. We keep on paying on a service that it’s not being served. The trial case in the court between these two are no longer beneficial to the community. This is being pending for so long already and until now it’s still a problem with no resolution. Our community resiliency are taken for granted.  How does our LGU takes this prolonged water crisis? Until when?

offices.name: Office of the City General Services Officer

events.content: Your feedback has been received by concerned office. Please wait for futher updates.

Good afternoon.

Thank you for bringing your concerns regarding the water service in our locality to our attention. We understand the challenges you are facing and would like to assure you that the City Government, the Sangguniang Panlungsod, and concerned offices, is actively engaging in dialogues and exploring all possible avenues to address this long-standing utility issue.

We would also like to inform you that PrimeWater is no longer in a joint venture with the Metro San Fernando Water District. Furthermore, as part of our commitment to securing a reliable water supply, City Mayor Hermenegildo A. Gualberto signed a Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) with the Korea Water Resources Corporation (K-Water) on January 27, 2026. The MOA initiates a feasibility study for a proposed bulk water supply and desalination facility, which we hope will provide a sustainable solution for our city.

Thank you for your patience and understanding as we work toward these long-term improvements.
This feedback is mark as completed. Thank You!

content:
Good day, City Government of San Fernando.

I would like to inquire regarding the Individual Working Permit (IWP) and Health Card issued by LEBDO.

I currently have a valid IWP and Health Card. However, I have already resigned from my previous employer (a food restaurant) and have recently been hired by another food restaurant, which also requires a Health Card.

May I ask if it is possible to simply update or change the name of the restaurant indicated on my existing Health Card, instead of applying for a new one from the beginning?

Since my IWP and Health Card are still valid, I am hoping that only the employer’s name can be changed without having to comply again with all the documentary and laboratory requirements, such as fecalysis, Barangay Clearance, Police Clearance, and other requirements.

I would appreciate your clarification on this matter. Thank you very much, and I look forward to your response.

offices.name: Office of the City Administrator
Office of the City Human Resources & Management

events.content: Your feedback has been received by concerned office. Please wait for futher updates.

Good day Kabsat Karl Jay!

Thank you for reaching out. We have noted your inquiry regarding the updating of the employer's name on your existing Individual Working Permit (IWP) and Health Card.

We will coordinate with the concerned office regarding your inquiry and provide you with an update as soon as we receive their response.

Thank you for your patience and understanding.
Your feedback has been received by concerned office. Please wait for futher updates.

Hi Sir Karl Jay,

Regarding your concern, here is the response from the concerned office.

If your Health Certificate is still valid and you only need to change the name of your employer/restaurant, you may apply for the replacement or updating of your Health Certificate. You only need to:

Pay the prescribed fee for the replacement/reissuance of the Health Certificate.;
Present a valid Stool/Fecalysis Examination Result (not more than six (6) months old);
Present a valid Food Handler's Seminar Certificate.

There is no need to undergo the entire application process again provided that your Health Certificate remains valid and your supporting documents comply with the requirements.

Thank you.
This feedback is mark as completed. Thank You!

content:
Subject: Complaint Regarding Tricycle Driver – Body No. 1435

I would like to file a complaint regarding a tricycle with Body Number 1435, which I rode from Pagudpud, San Fernando, La Union to the San Fernando Public Market.

The distance of the trip is approximately 4.5 kilometers. Based on the fare matrix that I understand to be applicable, the fare should be approximately ₱25, consisting of the ₱15 base fare plus the corresponding additional charge for the succeeding kilometers.

However, I voluntarily offered the driver ₱60, which is already more than twice the fare I understand to be applicable. I was willing to pay the additional amount because I understand the current difficulties faced by tricycle drivers, including the cost of fuel and the expenses involved in operating their vehicles.

Despite my willingness to pay ₱60, the driver still complained about the amount and appeared to expect a significantly higher fare, which I understood to be around ₱150. My concern is not simply the amount of money involved. My primary concern is the attitude and manner in which the driver dealt with me as a passenger, especially considering that I was already willing to pay substantially more than the fare I understood to be required.

I also noticed that the applicable fare matrix was not posted or displayed inside the tricycle. As a passenger, I believe that clearly displaying the approved fare matrix would help prevent misunderstandings and disputes regarding fares.

I fully understand that tricycle drivers need to earn a living and that fuel prices and operating expenses can affect them. This is precisely why I voluntarily offered ₱60 instead of insisting on paying only the fare I calculated from the fare matrix. However, I believe passengers should still be treated respectfully, and fare collection should be based on the applicable approved fare rather than an amount demanded by the driver.

I respectfully request that the concerned office:

1. Verify the current approved fare matrix applicable to the Pagudpud–San Fernando Public Market route;
2. Verify whether Tricycle Body No. 1435 is required to display the fare matrix inside the vehicle;
3. Look into the conduct and manner of the driver during the incident; and
4. Take whatever appropriate action is warranted under the applicable rules and regulations.

I am not seeking to unfairly penalize the driver. I simply want the incident properly investigated and for passengers and drivers alike to have a clear understanding of the applicable fare.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

content:
Formal Complaint: Deceptive Fee Practices & Exploitative Conduct by Allizon Car Aircon

On October 12, 2026, my pregnant wife visited Allizon Car Aircon in San Fernando City purely to inquire about pricing and request a cost estimate for car aircon servicing.

Without our consent or any prior disclosure of an inspection fee, the staff opened the vehicle hood to assess the issue and gave a quotation. When we decided to canvas elsewhere to compare prices, the shop insisted and forced my wife to pay an undisclosed ₱150 "check-up fee" before leaving.

We believe the shop exploited my wife’s situation—taking advantage of a pregnant customer whom they assumed lacked technical knowledge about auto repair to coerce payment for a basic price check.

We subsequently visited another local shop in San Fernando City, where we received a fair and transparent quote without being coerced or charged a fee just to ask for pricing.

We believe our rights to clear product/service information and freedom of choice were violated when an undisclosed ₱150 fee was imposed simply for requesting a price estimate, effectively penalizing us for canvassing.

We believe our rights as consumers were further compromised by predatory and deceptive practices that took advantage of my pregnant wife's situation to force payment for a service we never requested or agreed to.
